analysis:
I found no concrete regression in the supplied evidence. The key behavior is the new `cluster_runtime` step in `.github/workflows/release-provider.yml` (lines ~941-977). It runs `scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh` against the final signed app. Before running any repo code it deletes the signing keychain, proves the Developer ID identity is no longer listed, re-checks the bundle SHA-256 against the value recorded after final smoke, and unsets `r2_public_url` and `coordinator_url`. Notarization credentials appear only in the Notarize step env, and the release key and R2 secrets appear only in the later stage and publish jobs. This fits the Developer ID / release-key side of A-005, A-011 and A-017, and I saw no change that weakens the signing and notarization chain, the entitlement checks or the post-staple `cmp` checks.

The opt-in `CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND` (lines ~298-308) is true only for publishing runs when the per-environment variable is `true`. When it is true, the step fails closed because `continue-on-error` is false. When it is not true, failure only warns and the payload is unchanged (lines 1078-1088). The facts file is passed to `provider-release-publication.py prepare`.

Open integration points:
- I did not see `provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh`, `provider-cluster-runtime-models.py` or `provider-release-publication.py`. I could not verify that the facts script really runs the CLI with an empty environment, or that nothing sensitive reaches the facts JSON, step summary or the 30-day artifact (lines ~979-1022).
- I could not verify how the coordinator treats `cluster_runtime` as input to cluster approvals, pair-serving grants and parity qualifications. That is platform-owned and out of scope here. It does mean CI-computed facts become a trust input authenticated only by the release key, and those backend semantics are unreviewed.
- `GITHUB_ENV` may hold other secret-derived values that the step does not unset. This is unverified.

`release-swift.yml` (lines 66-67) only adds trigger path filters for the new scripts. The changelog is documentation only and has no security effect.
